items.front: In Amazon VPC, private instances must reach Amazon S3 without NAT processing charges. What do you use?
items.back: A gateway endpoint for Amazon S3.
items.extra: A gateway endpoint lets you [avoid the NAT Gateway Data Processing charge](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-gateway-endpoint-no-hourly-or-processing-charge) for Amazon S3 traffic.

items.front: In Amazon VPC, security group or network ACL: which one can deny one IP address?
items.back: The network ACL.
items.extra: A security group has [allow rules only](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-sg-vs-nacl-rule-type); a network ACL has [allow and deny rules](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-sg-vs-nacl-rule-type).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, security group or network ACL: which one needs its own rule for the reply traffic?
items.back: The network ACL. It is stateless.
items.extra: In a network ACL, return traffic [must be explicitly allowed (stateless)](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-sg-vs-nacl-return-traffic).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, can one subnet span two Availability Zones?
items.back: No. Each subnet lives in one Availability Zone.
items.extra: A subnet [must reside entirely within one Availability Zone](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-subnet-single-az). For high availability, create subnets in two or more zones.

items.front: In Amazon VPC, can you resize the existing CIDR block of a VPC?
items.back: No. Add a secondary CIDR block.
items.extra: You [cannot increase or decrease the size of an existing CIDR block](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-cidr-cannot-resize). The secondary block [must not overlap with any existing CIDR block that's associated with the VPC](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-cidr-cannot-resize).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, outbound internet access must survive the loss of one Availability Zone. What do you deploy?
items.back: A NAT gateway in each zone or one regional NAT gateway.
items.extra: With one shared zonal gateway, [resources in the other Availability Zones lose internet access](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-natgw-shared-across-azs-loses-internet). A regional NAT gateway [automatically expands across Availability Zones based on your workload presence](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-regional-natgw-vs-zonal).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, what makes a subnet public: an internet gateway attached to the VPC, or a route to it?
items.back: A route to the internet gateway in its route table.
items.extra: Without that route, [instances in the private subnet can't communicate with the internet, even if they have public IP addresses](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-vs-private-subnet-by-igw-route).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, can you associate a security group with a NAT gateway?
items.back: No. Use a network ACL on its subnet.
items.extra: [You can't associate a security group with a NAT gateway](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-natgw-no-security-group-use-nacl). [You can use a network ACL to control the traffic to and from the subnet for your NAT gateway](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-natgw-no-security-group-use-nacl).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, IPv6 instances need outbound-only internet access. What do you use?
items.back: An egress-only internet gateway.
items.extra: The egress-only internet gateway is [for use with IPv6 traffic only](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-eigw-ipv6-outbound-only). [To enable outbound-only internet communication over IPv4, use a NAT gateway instead](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-eigw-ipv6-outbound-only).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, flow logs or Traffic Mirroring: which one copies the packet contents?
items.back: Traffic Mirroring.
items.extra: Traffic Mirroring lets you [analyze actual traffic content, including payload](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-faq-flow-logs-vs-traffic-mirroring). Flow logs record addresses, ports, counts and accept or reject.

items.front: In Amazon VPC, can on-premises servers use an S3 gateway endpoint?
items.back: No. Use an interface endpoint.
items.extra: [Gateway endpoints do not allow access from on-premises networks, from peered VPCs in other AWS Regions, or through a transit gateway](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-gateway-endpoint-no-onprem-cross-region-tgw).

items.front: In Amazon VPC route tables, first match or longest prefix match: which rule picks the route?
items.back: Longest prefix match.
items.extra: A route table uses the most specific route that matches, the [longest prefix match](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-route-longest-prefix-match). First match is the rule of network ACLs.

items.front: In Amazon VPC, NAT gateway or NAT instance: which one supports port forwarding?
items.back: The NAT instance.
items.extra: For port forwarding, a NAT gateway is [not supported](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-natgw-vs-instance-port-forwarding). On a NAT instance, you [manually customize the configuration to support port forwarding](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-natgw-vs-instance-port-forwarding).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, an EC2 instance must work as a NAT instance. Which check do you turn off?
items.back: The source/destination check.
items.extra: [Each EC2 instance performs source/destination checks by default](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-nat-instance-disable-source-dest-check), so [you must disable source/destination checks on the NAT instance](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-nat-instance-disable-source-dest-check).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, can you get back an automatic public IPv4 address after it is released?
items.back: No. Use an Elastic IP address.
items.extra: An automatic public IPv4 address is [released back into the pool, and is no longer available for you to use](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ip-from-amazon-pool-released).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, is a public IPv4 address on a running instance free of charge?
items.back: No. In use or idle, the price is the same.
items.extra: [You pay an hourly rate for each public IPv4 address used by your AWS account](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ipv4-hourly-in-use-or-idle). [The price is the same whether the public IPv4 address is in-use](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-public-ipv4-hourly-in-use-or-idle) or idle.

items.front: In Amazon VPC, does a network ACL filter traffic between two instances in the same subnet?
items.back: No. Use security groups for that traffic.
items.extra: Network ACLs [do not filter traffic between instances in the same subnet](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-faq-network-acl-same-subnet).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, zonal or regional NAT gateway: which one needs no public subnet?
items.back: The regional NAT gateway.
items.extra: For a regional NAT gateway, [you don't need to create a public subnet to host it](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-regional-natgw-no-public-subnet).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, can a regional NAT gateway do private NAT?
items.back: No. Use a zonal NAT gateway.
items.extra: Regional NAT gateways [do not support private NAT](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-regional-nat-no-private-nat).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, the NAT gateway metric ErrorPortAllocation is above zero. What does it mean?
items.back: Too many concurrent connections through the NAT gateway.
items.extra: A value above zero means that [too many concurrent connections are open through the NAT gateway](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-natgw-metric-errorportallocation).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, does removing a security group rule stop its tracked connections at once?
items.back: No. They continue until they time out.
items.extra: After a rule change, [its tracked connections are not immediately interrupted](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-sg-rule-change-tracked-connections-continue). To cut traffic at once, [you can use a network ACL for your subnet](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-sg-rule-change-tracked-connections-continue).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, a database must accept only the web tier, whose IP addresses change. What is the rule's source?
items.back: The web tier's security group ID.
items.extra: The source of a security group rule can be [the ID of a security group](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-sg-rule-sources).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, can you delete the main route table of a VPC?
items.back: No. You can change its routes.
items.extra: You [can't delete the main route table](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-main-route-table-rules), but you can add, remove and change its routes.

items.front: In Amazon VPC, a subnet has no explicit route table association. Which route table does it use?
items.back: The main route table.
items.extra: Without an explicit association, [the subnet is implicitly associated with the main route table](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-route-table-implicit-main-association).

items.front: In Amazon VPC data transfer over private IP addresses, same Availability Zone or another zone: which one is free?
items.back: The same zone, over private IP addresses.
items.extra: Data transfer within one Availability Zone [is free irrespective of account ownership of the communicating resources](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-sharing-same-az-transfer-free). Traffic between zones is charged per gigabyte. Over public addresses the Regional rate applies when [Public or Elastic IP addresses are used, regardless of which Availability Zone the other instance is in](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-data-transfer-public-ip-regional-rate).

items.front: In Amazon VPC, the largest IPv4 CIDR block of a VPC is a {{c1::/16 netmask (65,536 IP addresses)}}.
In Amazon VPC, every subnet reserves {{c1::the first four (4) IP addresses}} and the last one.
In a network ACL, to cover every client type, you {{c1::open ephemeral ports 1024-65535}} for the replies.
In Amazon VPC, a zonal NAT gateway scales {{c1::up to 100 Gbps}}.
In Amazon VPC, each IPv4 address of a NAT gateway supports {{c1::55,000 simultaneous connections}} to one destination.
In Amazon VPC, the default quota is {{c1::5 VPCs per Region}}.
In Amazon VPC, you can attach {{c1::only one internet gateway to a VPC at a time}}.
